1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The branch and the pull request were chosen for you
11	
12	**Push to the `Target-branch:` your item carries, and onto the `Target-pr:` where it
13	carries one.** The executor resolved both from the task's `expected_outcome` before
14	your session started: `fresh_pr` gave you a new branch and left the task's earlier pull
15	requests alone; `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` gave you the branch of the task's
16	newest open pull request, or a fresh one only where the task had no open pull request
17	at all; `supersede_existing_pr` gave you a fresh branch and listed the earlier ones under
18	`Supersedes:`. Where there is a `Target-pr:`, push onto it and open nothing — the pull
19	request already exists and your push updates it. Where there is none, open your pull
20	request on that branch. Never mint a branch name, never search for an open pull
21	request to reuse, and never close an earlier run's pull request yourself: the converge
22	(`src/session/converge-item.mjs`, handed `--pr`) closes what `Supersedes:` names once yours
23	exists, and a run that delivered nothing leaves them where they were.
24	
25	**A `Target-pr:` that conflicts with its base is yours to resolve, not to walk away
26	from.** Merge the base branch into the target branch, resolve the conflicts, and carry
27	on with your own work on top - a task told to amend has no prerogative to open a second
28	pull request, and one that forks leaves the first open and accumulating beside the
29	second. If you cannot resolve it, stop and say so in your wrap-up comment: a parked item
30	naming the conflict is a correct outcome, and a second pull request is not one.
31	
32	## Say which task wrote it
33	
34	**Every commit you push on a task's behalf carries `Claudinite-Task: <pack>/<task>` on
35	its own line** — the pack and task id from the work item's first line. When you merge,
36	put the same line in the squash commit's message too: the merge commit is what lands on
37	the default branch, and it is the one the signal collectors read.
38	
39	That trailer is how the scheduler tells the project moving from the machinery running. A
40	task's own delivery must never count as the repo activity that wakes the next task, and
41	a title is not a reliable way to say so — every new task's title is a new leak. Yours
42	says it in the commit.
43	
44	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
45	
46	Your task's declared `automerge` is a **ceiling, not a plan**.
47	On a request item the authorization is the item's **`Merge:` field** instead,
48	read within that ceiling: absent means `nothing`, `if-narrow` means the
49	`narrow-diff` composite, and any other value is the policy expression itself.
50	Whichever source it came from:
51	
52	- **`nothing`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
53	  applies to you.
54	- **`anything`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
55	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
56	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
57	- **a policy list** (e.g. `['comment-only-changes', 'readme-changes']`, a folder
58	  scope such as `['under:product-wiki']`, or an intersection of the two,
59	  `['under:product-wiki && doc-changes']`) — the task may
60	  land its PR only when the diff sits inside the policy, and the policy engine decides
61	  that, never your reading of the diff. Before step 2, run it from the repository root —
62	  `src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the claudinite-tasks pack (probe
63	  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs`, falling back to
64	  `packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the canon):
65	
66	  ```
67	  node <that file> --base <the PR's base branch> --policy '<the terms, ;-joined>'
68	  ```
69	
70	  `AUTOMERGE: no` — leave the PR open for review, quote the verdict line in your wrap-up,
71	  and stop; a diff wider than its policy waiting for a person is a correct outcome, and
72	  you never re-shape a change to fit the classifier. `AUTOMERGE: yes` — amend your
73	  branch's final commit to carry the arming trailer on its own line,
74	  `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: <the same expression>`, push, and continue below (the
75	  `automerge-policy-scope` check re-measures the diff against the trailer, so a
76	  mis-measured arm goes red instead of merging).
77	
78	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
79	
80	`.claudinite-settings.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
81	
82	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
83	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
84	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading an
85	  authorized landing to review is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
86	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
87	  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
88	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
89	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
90	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.
91	
92	## 2. Arm auto-merge
93	
94	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
95	it once this repo's required checks pass.
96	
97	## 3. When the arm is rejected
98	
99	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
100	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
101	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
102	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
103	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
104	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
105	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
106	  PR's **head sha**:
107	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
108	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
109	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
110	    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
111	  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
112	    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
113	    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
114	    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
115	    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
116	    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
117	    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the ceiling — the trail
118	    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
119	    unseen check does not survive anything.
120	
121	## Never
122	
123	Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
124	arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
125	manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
126	are always legal outcomes.
127

request on that branch. Never mint a branch name, never search for an open pull
request to reuse, and never close an earlier run's pull request yourself: the converge
(`src/session/converge-item.mjs`, handed `--pr`) closes what `Supersedes:` names once yours
exists, and a run that delivered nothing leaves them where they were.

**A `Target-pr:` that conflicts with its base is yours to resolve, not to walk away
from.** Merge the base branch into the target branch, resolve the conflicts, and carry
on with your own work on top - a task told to amend has no prerogative to open a second
pull request, and one that forks leaves the first open and accumulating beside the
second. If you cannot resolve it, stop and say so in your wrap-up comment: a parked item
naming the conflict is a correct outcome, and a second pull request is not one.

## Say which task wrote it

**Every commit you push on a task's behalf carries `Claudinite-Task: <pack>/<task>` on
its own line** — the pack and task id from the work item's first line. When you merge,
put the same line in the squash commit's message too: the merge commit is what lands on
the default branch, and it is the one the signal collectors read.

That trailer is how the scheduler tells the project moving from the machinery running. A
task's own delivery must never count as the repo activity that wakes the next task, and
a title is not a reliable way to say so — every new task's title is a new leak. Yours
says it in the commit.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `automerge` is a **ceiling, not a plan**.
On a request item the authorization is the item's **`Merge:` field** instead,
read within that ceiling: absent means `nothing`, `if-narrow` means the
`narrow-diff` composite, and any other value is the policy expression itself.
Whichever source it came from:

- **`nothing`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`anything`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
- **a policy list** (e.g. `['comment-only-changes', 'readme-changes']`, a folder
  scope such as `['under:product-wiki']`, or an intersection of the two,
  `['under:product-wiki && doc-changes']`) — the task may
  land its PR only when the diff sits inside the policy, and the policy engine decides
  that, never your reading of the diff. Before step 2, run it from the repository root —
  `src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the claudinite-tasks pack (probe
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs`, falling back to
  `packs/claudinite-tasks/src/session/merge-policy-run.mjs` in the canon):

  ```
  node <that file> --base <the PR's base branch> --policy '<the terms, ;-joined>'
  ```

  `AUTOMERGE: no` — leave the PR open for review, quote the verdict line in your wrap-up,
  and stop; a diff wider than its policy waiting for a person is a correct outcome, and
  you never re-shape a change to fit the classifier. `AUTOMERGE: yes` — amend your
  branch's final commit to carry the arming trailer on its own line,
  `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: <the same expression>`, push, and continue below (the
  `automerge-policy-scope` check re-measures the diff against the trailer, so a
  mis-measured arm goes red instead of merging).

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-settings.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading an
  authorized landing to review is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
  PR's **head sha**:
  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the ceiling — the trail
    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
    unseen check does not survive anything.

## Never

Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
are always legal outcomes.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/committing

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking. (concern-commit)
- **Reference the issue, when the change has one** — `Refs #n`, or `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n` where
  the commit finishes it. A change tracked by its PR alone references nothing.
  (reference-issue-change)
- **A landed commit is revised by a new commit**, never a rewrite of that one.
  (landed-commit-revised)
- **Stage by name** — `git add <paths>` for the files this commit is about; `-a` sweeps in whatever
  else was in progress. (stage-name)

input.title: provenance.mjs answers from the clone's horizon on a shallow checkout
input.body:
Six history walks in `packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs` ask git for an earliest commit with no range bound and no shallow probe, so on a shallow checkout they answer with the clone's own horizon rather than saying they cannot answer:

- `:158` `log --reverse -S**(<key>)**` - a rule's birth date
- `:251` `log -S<text>` - the carrier follow
- `:519` `log --reverse --raw` - the per-path commit walk
- `:587` `rev-list --reverse --topo-order HEAD` - commit positions
- `:603` `log --reverse` over a path set
- `:634` `log --reverse -S| <version> |` - the version-log row

The failure is silent: the brief comes back empty or short and reads as "this element has no history". Two subagent dispatches on 2026-09-22 (#2263, #2267) had to compensate by hand, each telling its agent to run `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and `git fetch --unshallow` before trusting any brief. `packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-review/read-live.mjs` shows the shape that works: probe, and return "not knowable" rather than the horizon's answer.

**What to do:** probe once and fail loudly (or deepen with `git fetch --unshallow`) before the walks, so a shallow checkout reports that it cannot answer instead of answering wrongly.

`history-search-on-shallow-clone` in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/declared-checks.json` reports these six today. It carries `since: '2026-09-23'`, so it is advisory until **2026-10-07** and blocking after - this wants closing before then.

input.title: Claudinite growth: extract lessons
input.head: claudinite/claudinite-growth/growth-extract/2026-09-23-apemsr
input.body:
The growth-extract run over the 2026-09-22 window — 13 substantive commits, the pull requests merged in it, and 18 fresh conversation captures plus the 6 oldest still on the branch. Two lessons cleared the bar; one landed as a check.

Refs #2271

## `history-search-on-shallow-clone` — a declared world check

A `log`/`rev-list` pickaxe or `--reverse` walk with no `<ref>..<ref>` range answers with the earliest commit the **checkout reaches**, so on a shallow clone it hands back the clone's own horizon as the repository's history.

Evidence, both from this window:

- **#2244** fixed exactly this in `packDeclaredAt`: *"`git log --reverse -S` returns the earliest commit the checkout REACHES, so the adoption window started at the clone's horizon and one review over one record found different things on two checkouts."*
- The same day, the two provenance-backfill dispatches (**#2263**, **#2267**) each had to warn their subagent by hand — *"Verify history depth first… A shallow clone silently produces an empty brief"* — because `provenance.mjs` does not probe.

Scope over the real tree: **6 findings, all in `packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs`, nothing else**. `tasks/usage-review/read-live.mjs` is silent because it probes; `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs` is silent because its `--reverse` walk is bounded by `${mergeBase()}..HEAD`. Those two exclusions are what the fixture pair proves — weakening either `unless` turns the clean case red.

`since: '2026-09-23'`, so it is advisory until 2026-10-07 and blocking after. The backlog it surfaces is **#2277**, filed for it — this run may not touch `packs/`.

## `test-derives-answer` — widened from tests to code

The rule read *"A test that derives its answer by walking git history"*. The window's own failure was in a tool, not a test, and the three history-reading tools here sat outside it. The trigger is now *"Deriving an answer by walking git history"*, in a test or a tool alike.

This is the one rule the change deliberately re-titles, so **`rules-append-only` reports it as removed** (advisory) — it is a rewording, not a retirement.

## `changing-guidance-produced` — new prose

From the owner on **#2250**: after rewriting the provenance guidance, *"try to test them in a new subagent, by deleting the changes in 2250, and asking it to fix 2245 from scratch, and then review the output provenance it created."*

That is the see-it-fail the prose rung otherwise has none of. The upgrade pass **declined to convert it**: its trigger is a judgment ("guidance that produced a bad artifact"), and a work rule reading "prose edited, no Agent dispatch" would fire on every rewording and guess intent. Recorded on `_declined.md`.

## Declined, and why

- **Promoting `pipe-tail-hides-exit` out of advisory** — it fired in five of the window's captures, several calls each, and no session acted on it. The check is canon `basics`', outside this run's write surface; the severity call is the usage-review's.
- **A shape for state-transition tables** — #2262's owner reshaped one table over three rounds. How a summary is shaped is the owner's own preference, injected per session; a pack copy goes stale silently.

## Hindsight window

The oldest 24h on the logs branch (2026-07-19/20) yielded nothing new: pack independence via barriers is `wanting-rule-packs`, the reversed standing decision is `owner-reversing-standing`, and "don't mention things outside the pack" is `describing-another-packs`.

## Verification

- Suite: **3925 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking**, 25 advisory — 6 of them this check's new backlog, the other 19 pre-existing in `packs/node`, `packs/basics` and `packs/git-github`.
- `check_the_work`: **0 blocking**, 1 advisory — the deliberate re-title above.
- The new check seen red on a violating fixture and silent on both clean ones, with the guards mutated to confirm the clean case bites.

Two lessons cleared the bar; one landed as a check.

Refs #2271

## `history-search-on-shallow-clone` — a declared world check

A `log`/`rev-list` pickaxe or `--reverse` walk with no `<ref>..<ref>` range answers with the earliest commit the **checkout reaches**, so on a shallow clone it hands back the clone's own horizon as the repository's history.

Evidence, both from this window:

- **#2244** fixed exactly this in `packDeclaredAt`: *"`git log --reverse -S` returns the earliest commit the checkout REACHES, so the adoption window started at the clone's horizon and one review over one record found different things on two checkouts."*
- The same day, the two provenance-backfill dispatches (**#2263**, **#2267**) each had to warn their subagent by hand — *"Verify history depth first… A shallow clone silently produces an empty brief"* — because `provenance.mjs` does not probe.

Scope over the real tree: **6 findings, all in `packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs`, nothing else**. `tasks/usage-review/read-live.mjs` is silent because it probes; `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs` is silent because its `--reverse` walk is bounded by `${mergeBase()}..HEAD`. Those two exclusions are what the fixture pair proves — weakening either `unless` turns the clean case red.

`since: '2026-09-23'`, so it is advisory until 2026-10-07 and blocking after. The backlog it surfaces is **#2277**, filed for it — this run may not touch `packs/`.

## `test-derives-answer` — widened from tests to code

The rule read *"A test that derives its answer by walking git history"*. The window's own failure was in a tool, not a test, and the three history-reading tools here sat outside it. The trigger is now *"Deriving an answer by walking git history"*, in a test or a tool alike.

This is the one rule the change deliberately re-titles, so **`rules-append-only` reports it as removed** (advisory) — it is a rewording, not a retirement.

## `changing-guidance-produced` — new prose

From the owner on **#2250**: after rewriting the provenance guidance, *"try to test them in a new subagent, by deleting the changes in 2250, and asking it to fix 2245 from scratch, and then review the output provenance it created."*

That is the see-it-fail the prose rung otherwise has none of. The upgrade pass **declined to convert it**: its trigger is a judgment ("guidance that produced a bad artifact"), and a work rule reading "prose edited, no Agent dispatch" would fire on every rewording and guess intent. Recorded on `_declined.md`.

## Declined, and why

- **Promoting `pipe-tail-hides-exit` out of advisory** — it fired in five of the window's captures, several calls each, and no session acted on it. The check is canon `basics`', outside this run's write surface; the severity call is the usage-review's.
- **A shape for state-transition tables** — #2262's owner reshaped one table over three rounds. How a summary is shaped is the owner's own preference, injected per session; a pack copy goes stale silently.

## Hindsight window

The oldest 24h on the logs branch (2026-07-19/20) yielded nothing new: pack independence via barriers is `wanting-rule-packs`, the reversed standing decision is `owner-reversing-standing`, and "don't mention things outside the pack" is `describing-another-packs`.

## Verification

- Suite: **3925 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking**, 25 advisory — 6 of them this check's new backlog, the other 19 pre-existing in `packs/node`, `packs/basics` and `packs/git-github`.
- `check_the_work`: **0 blocking**, 1 advisory — the deliberate re-title above.
- The new check seen red on a violating fixture and silent on both clean ones, with the guards mutated to confirm the clean case bites.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```

Two lessons out of the 2026-09-22 window, one of them as a check.

`history-search-on-shallow-clone` is a declared world check over `.mjs`: a
`log`/`rev-list` pickaxe or `--reverse` with no `<ref>..<ref>` range, in a file
that never probes `--is-shallow-repository`, answers with the earliest commit
the CHECKOUT reaches. #2244 fixed exactly that in `packDeclaredAt`, and the same
day two subagent dispatches had to warn by hand that a shallow clone empties
`provenance.mjs brief`. It fires on six lines there and nowhere else. The
backlog is #2277, due before the `since` grace closes on 2026-10-07.

`test-derives-answer` named only tests, so every history-reading tool here sat
outside it; its trigger widens to "Deriving an answer by walking git history".

`changing-guidance-produced` is new prose: prove a rewritten guidance by
deleting the artifact it produced and having a fresh subagent redo the task
against the new text. The upgrade pass declined to convert it.

Refs #2271

Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: under:.claudinite/local
Claudinite-Task: claudinite-growth/growth-extract
